svg.title: A client is 3 hr out from a lumbar puncture. The client reports a throbbing headache that gets worse on sitting up and eases when lying flat . The puncture site is dry and intact with no drainage. Neurologic checks are unchanged, temperature 37.0 C (98.6 F), and the client has taken only a few sips of water since the test.
svg.desc: A headache that is worse upright and better flat after a lumbar puncture is caused by cerebrospinal fluid leaking from the needle site. Staying flat and drinking fluids lowers the pressure difference and supports fluid replacement, so that is the first action. Sitting up or walking makes the leak headache worse, and withholding fluids works against replacing what was lost. If it does not resolve, an epidural blood patch seals the leak; there is no sign of herniation here, and draining more fluid would deepen the problem.
